cases.note: Rate::try_round_u64 rounded half-up, and CollateralExchangeRate::collateral_to_liquidity and liquidity_to_collateral both used it. Converting between collateral and liquidity therefore rounded in the depositor's favour, so an amount chosen to sit just above a half-unit boundary came back worth more than it went in, and the difference was paid out of the reserve. Repeated, that drains the pool one rounding unit at a time. The fix floors both conversions with try_floor_u64, so rounding always favours the protocol, removes try_round_u64 from Rate entirely, and applies the minimum borrow fee in Decimal before rounding rather than after.

cases.note: Program<'info, System> skipped its own program-id check. The untyped Program<'info, ()> shorthand was implemented by giving () an Id of Pubkey::default(), used as a sentinel meaning 'do not check the id', and Pubkey::default() is the System program's own address. System::id() therefore collided with the sentinel, so any executable account passed in that slot was accepted as the System program. The fix deletes the sentinel and gives Program<'info, ()> its own TryFrom that skips the key check by construction, so the typed path always compares the key.

cases.note: process_deposit transferred the user's SOL to whatever account occupied the reserve_account slot and minted stSOL in proportion, without ever checking that the slot held the real reserve. The fix adds one line that re-derives the reserve program-derived address from the program id and the Solido instance address and rejects any account whose key does not match.

cases.note: SellRewards is permissionless and built an spl_token_swap swap instruction whose program id came straight from a caller-supplied account, then invoke_signed it with the Anker reserve authority PDA seeds, handing an attacker's program a signature over the reserve. The fix does not hardcode a program id, which would break multi-cluster testing; it requires that the program about to be invoked is the owner of the swap-pool state account, and the swap-pool address is stored in Anker's state and changeable only by the manager.

cases.note: Fee::apply computed amt * numerator / denominator with integer division, which floors. Any operation small enough that amt * numerator was below the denominator paid exactly zero fee, so splitting an operation into many small ones avoided the fee entirely. The fix switches to ceiling division so any non-zero chargeable amount pays at least one.

cases.note: process_approve_account for the confidential-transfer extension unpacked a token account and, separately, a mint account, then applied the mint's confidential-transfer authority to the token account without establishing that the two belonged together. An attacker could present a token account for one mint alongside a mint they control and self-approve. The fix compares the mint account's key against the token account's own mint before any of the mint's configuration is read.

cases.note: MPL refuses to sign for a foreign program under the special authority index 0 by comparing ix.program_id against its own program id. The bypass is to aim the instruction at MPL itself: a nested execute_transaction passes that check trivially, and Solana carries the parent's PDA signatures into the child, so a third level reaches an attacker contract holding both. The fix blacklists the execute_transaction and execute_instruction discriminators from being the target of a 0-authority execution.

cases.note: The stake pool mints pool tokens against SOL at an exchange rate that assumes both sides use 9 decimals, because that is native_mint::DECIMALS. A pool initialised with a mint of, say, 6 decimals leaves every conversion between lamports and pool tokens off by a factor of a thousand. The fix rejects a non-9-decimal mint at initialisation, which is the only place it can be fixed because the mint cannot be changed afterwards.

cases.note: Account<T>'s safety story is that the owner is checked once during account validation. reload() exists precisely to re-read an account after a CPI, which is exactly the window in which ownership can have changed, so re-deserialising the bytes without re-checking the owner leaves a program trusting T-shaped data in an account now owned by somebody else. The fix moves reload() into the T: Owner impl block and re-runs the owner check inside it.
